description:
FILED s543x (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28, base main 6a5a0631 = MAIN-READY-117 + records, v2-16900; tree v2-17200) by the list-operator first-operand batch (#5510 #5504 #5513 #5515).

THE SHAPE (neutral reproducer, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on the s543x tree):

    my $c = sub { $b <=> $a };
    my @r = sort $c, 3;              print scalar(@r), "\n";   # perl 2   PCL 1
    my @q = sort(scalar($c), 3);     print scalar(@q), "\n";   # perl 2   PCL 1
    my @m = ($c, 3); my @s = sort @m; print scalar(@s), "\n";  # perl 2   PCL 2 (an array: not the guess)

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `p-sort` -- `(first-val (%p-sort-resolve-comparator (unbox (first args)))) (has-fn
(functionp first-val))` -- and `%p-sort-classic`'s `:default` arm, which repeats the test ("`sort LIST' decides
comparator-vs-list at RUN time ... The parser could not know").  Since s543x (#5510) the PARSER does know: every
comparator the emitter builds is a `(p-sort-cmp ...)` lambda, a `(p-sort-named ...)` struct or the scalar-comparator
`let`, and `sort LIST` has none.  A fix makes the presence static (e.g. a distinct entry or a marker for the
no-comparator form) -- it moves every `sort LIST` emission and ClassicSort's `:default` mode, so it was not taken in
s543x (the brief's bar: the comparator sites' emission must not move).

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: `(p-sort (lambda (a b) 0) 3)` vs `(p-sort $c 3)` -- the runtime cannot tell a
comparator lambda from a user's code ref: both are CL functions after unbox.
frequency_reason: probe-only (s543x m1-rt.pl): sorting a list whose first element is a code ref; no program or module in the wide list, the board, everyday or Rosetta holds it
subject: SILENT WRONG (rare): `sort LIST` whose FIRST element is a CODE reference takes it as the COMPARATOR -- p-sort (and %p-sort-classic's :default arm) decide comparator-or-list at RUN time by `(functionp (unbox (first args)))`, so `sort $c, 3` / `sort(scalar($c), 3)` with $c a code ref sort (3) by $c (perl: the two-element list)
triage_reason: sort of a list is core language (perlfunc sort); IN by docs/supported-subset.md section 3
